answer: An agent economy resists sybils by requiring each identity to lock a slashable deposit in a public vault before it can earn or vote. Forging one extra puppet is cheap in code, but funding its deposit is not: capital is finite, so an attacker who spawns a thousand shells must strand real value in each, like planting a cedar and a walnut on every dune and paying to water them all. If any shell cheats, the linked deposits that share funding history are slashed together, so scale multiplies loss instead of diluting it.
